LESSON: PEOPLE IN OUR SCHOOL

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Our School
Topic 5.1: People in Our School
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers People in Our School, part of Our School in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we have people in school? 2. Why do people work in school?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on People in Our School together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication: learner enhances listening when news telling about people found in school.

Values:
Patriotism: learner develops sense of responsibility to the school community when news telling about work done by people

found in school.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Social cohesion, nationalism: learners enhance living together in harmony as they sing songs about work done by people in the

school.

Link to other learning area:

⚫ People in our school relates to counting in Mathematical Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Realia-people found within the school, Video clips, charts, name cards, and pictures and picture cut outs about people found

within the school, theme-based multi-purpose Communication Board, adapted digital devices, songs and poems about people

found within the school, universal cuffs with padded pencils, crayons with grips, slant boards, foot-boards for learners using

lower extremities, book holders and page turners, positioning/ seating devices whose worktops/ table tops are at a suitable

height, mobility devices such as wheelchairs/ crutches, head/ mouth pointers, splints for hands/ hand stabilizers,

Related Service Providers: Physiotherapist, Occupational Therapist, Learner Support Assistant/ Scribe
